steps.text: Place chicken breasts and broth in to a stockpot or Dutch oven. Bring to a boil and let simmer for about 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through. Remove the chicken from the broth and set aside to cool.

Put the leeks and carrots into the pot and simmer them for 10 minutes, or until tender. Shred the cooled chicken in to bite sized pieces and return it to the pot. Add the cabbage and egg noodles and cook another 5 minutes or until the noodles are soft. The soup should be thick like a stew. Serve hot and flavor to taste with Thai chili sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Thai Chicken Cabbage Soup
raw_recipe.description: This is a low-fat, low-cal soup that’s incredibly filling and delicious. I eat this at least once a week! I don’t know how it tastes cold, though. Don’t be afraid to vary the proportions of various foods on your own!

review.reviewBody: This was pretty good...my first time trying anything with leeks! I think it tastes best with half regular green cabbage and half Chinese napa cabbage. I used at least 2 tablespoons of chile sauce, which I added just after the noodles. I may cut back on the amount of noodles next time because after a day or two they absorbed all the juice. I'll continue making this recipe from time to time. **UPDATE** It's been a couple of years since I made this soup and now I've tried it again and made additional discoveries. First, if you're using spicy garlic sauce, two teaspoons will suffice and add 1 tablespoon of brown sugar. If you're using sweet garlic sauce, use 1 tablespoon and add a dash or two cayenne pepper. Secondly, to avoid loosing all the broth to the noodles, cook the noodles separately, then add them to the soup after the cabbage is just about tender, plus an additional cup of broth and 1 cup of water. Trust me; you'll love it!

Next time will cut carrots a bit smaller (I think mine were just on the large side), use a little less cabbage (mine was also on the large side), and pre cook the noodles (to save from soaking up the broth). Fixed this in Ninja Foodi and it was awesome. About three spoonfuls of the Thai Sweet Chili Sauce was spot on for a good sized bowl!

so i hate to review this because i changed it a bit(i am giving this 4 stars because as written it wouldn't be considered thai and very bland)...but mine ended up really good. this is what i did-
started with boiling chicken and water-added 1 .5 stalks 3 tablespoons lemon grass chopped fine, 1 tsp. fresh ginger,thai chili paste 3 tablespoons and 2 beef bouillon - (in another pan i sauteed 1 onion and 2 garlic cloves and added that to the soup mixture) then took out chicken shredded added it back with 3 cups cabbage, chopped tomato, carrot cut julienne, 3 tablespoons of cilantro. then let this simmer for 3 hours. about 30 mins. before serving i added 1 more cup shredded cabbage. and fresh cilantro. this was good and i added quite a bit of the thai chili paste because we like it spicy. this would be really good with shrimp in place of chicken as well!

I would make it again but, as suggested by other reviewers. would decrease the noodles by half and doubling the broth volume, add a stalk of lemongrass, 2 tbs garlic chili sauce, 2 tsp ginger, cilantro, 1T. soy sauce, and consider substituting shrimp for the chicken.

I made this for a Wednesday meal at church and it received rave reviews. I did make some changes. I added fish sauce, ginger, lemon grass and sesame oil as suggested by other reviewers. I bought a cold roasted chicken(lemon herb flavor) from grocery store, pulled off meat and made the stock with the bones. Since it was going to be kept warm over a long period of time I didn't use the noodles. They would have soaked up all the broth. Everyone said it tasted like soup from the Chinese restaurant. I will definitely make this soup again.

Very good. I used the same ingredients but altered the methods. Sauteed (well-seasoned) boneless, skinless, chicken breast instead of boiling. Personal preference, just don't care for boiled chicken, plus, I wanted to cook some extra chicken for future meals. Then I sauteed the leeks and carrots in the same pan, added the broth, brought to a boil, and then added the noodles and cabbage. I used cole slaw mix for the cabbage...so hard to figure out how much to use, tho. I really liked this soup...will become a regular for me! 09/28/15 Half of a small head of cabbage equals six cups..sounds like enuf, proportionally, for eight cups of broth, for six servings. Also added a few ribs of celery to this batch! Next time I will use fewer noodles. I added four additional cups of broth and still had very little liquid. 12/12/16 1 onion, 4 carrots, 2 ribs celery, 10 oz angel hair cole slaw mix, 8 cups Sam's chicken 'bone broth', 6 oz noodles...haven't added the chicken yet, but looks good so far. I know that the submitters said stew-like, but this (with these proportions) looks plenty thick for me!

I think this makes an excellent soup except that as written, the recipe produces a bland, except for heat from chilies, soup. I used garlic chili sauce, 2 to 3 times what was called for, but heat doesn't equal taste. When reheating leftovers, I added small amounts of fish sauce, lemon, and sesame oil. The result was perfect. I also recommend cooking the noodles separately as many other commenters have suggested.c

I followed some of the suggestions on this site and added fish sauce, red chili paste, sliced garlic and ginger to cook with the chicken. I left out the noodles, I spooned the soup over rice noodles when I served it. Over all, I will make it again.

This was delicious. I did add a few things just based on reviews, my personal preference & what I had on hand. Used 4 cups of chicken broth and 4 cups of lime/chile flavored chicken broth. Added minced ginger (about 3 slices. Added a stalk of young bok choy & half a head of green cabbage, a small package of snow peas, green onions & carrots. Towards the end of the simmering time I added about 1 TBSP of fish sauce & 1 TBSP of chile garlic sauce (the one with the green lid). I left out the noodles all together. It was wonderful, just enough spice & zip and super healthy!!!

I received the recipe in my email today and made it this evening. My husband and I loved it. I had already thawed a large bone-in chicken breast and had some fresh Savoy cabbage already cut up in the fridge. I didn't have any leeks, so I stirred in half a package of Knorr's leek soup mix (I think this sent it over the top!). I made half the recipe because I wasn't sure I'd like it. I didn't have Thai chili sauce, so I made some from scratch from another recipe on the website. This was easy and quick, and right on time for me as I am battling a cold, and what's better for a cold than chicken soup?

We really liked this. The textures were great. I read the reviews and made some of the adjustments mentioned. I added garlic, cayenne pepper, red pepper flakes, white pepper. I added some cilantro to garnish. I didn't have the thai chili sauce the recipe called for so I improvised and used a red taco sauce and some sweet hot pepper jelly I had on hand. We loved it this way but I bet its great with the Thai Chili Sauce too and will try it next time with that.
Easy and quick prep and a great meal during these cold days. Thanks!
Yes I made it with beef stock and added saugage instead of chicken. Followed everything thing else but added some Korean chili spice paste instead of tomatoes. Was delicious!
I love this recipe and i make it often

I read a bunch of reviews before making this. Noodles were never going to work as I had a very full pot. Nonetheless, this recipe was a base for a very tasty & hearty soup. I followed the instructions but added 4 stalks of celery and a thin sliced small white onion, 2tbsp fish sauce, 1tbsp dried cilantro, 1tbsp dried garlic, 2 tsp dried ginger. This was a last minute recipe so I didn't have time to get the aforementioned ingredients fresh. In the last 10 minutes of cooking I added 2 tbsp of the garlic chili paste (the one with the green lid) and I squeezed the juice of 3 limes into the broth. All I can say is wow! Try your own thing using this recipe as a base and see what happens. I didn't give the recipe 5 stars because if I had made it as its written I would not have liked it as much.

Super easy! Very filling and tasty. I cut the recipe into thirds as I only had one chicken breast at the time. I recommend adding the chili sauce a teaspoon at a time so you don't overdo. I like it spicy, so for my 1/3 recipe I ended up adding about a tablespoon.

IT WAS A FINE CABBAGE AND CHICKEN SOUP. NOT SURE WHAT MAKES IT THAI. 
 SUGGESTIONS, RECEIPE CALLS FOR "SHREDDED" CABBAGE BUT SHOULD REALLY E CHOPPED. ALSO, I FOUND THE EGG NOODLE TO BE RATHER UNNECESSARY TO THE SOUP. THAI CHILI IS OPTIONAL BUT NECESSARY. MAYBE A DIFFERENT TYPE OF CABBAGE? A BIT OF PEPPER FLAKES. I'D EXPERIMENT WITH THIS BASIC RECIPT.
Add, subtract. It’s all good.
Liked it b/c was easy & quick to make with lots of flavour. A perfect Covid19 day at home comfort food experience.
I will most defiantly make this again . I love my meals with a like more kick to it so I added some chili spice to it and it was out of this world.
